originalGroup.material:
Heavy Backpack Story 035B

Before a short hill walk, Dima filled his backpack with things he loved: a thick comic, a model car, a holiday stone and a drawing folder. There was little space left for water and a raincoat. He did not want to leave anything behind because each object reminded him of a good day.
His grandma did not tell him the objects were useless. She asked what the walk required and where the other objects could wait safely. Dima put the model and folder on his shelf, with a note to finish his drawing later. He kept the small stone in one pocket. With water and a raincoat packed, the bag was still lighter than before. On the hill, he was glad he could walk comfortably. Choosing for one journey had not meant giving up everything he cared about.
